done_when: forge land on a fix with no commits beyond its start and state records runs forge work first, and it merges only after the builder round. A fix whose real work is only Forge's records can still merge when it has a work commit.

known.title: Preserve completed native rounds before starting another build

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional
Case: normal use - a native Codex or Claude builder finishes without making a commit, then the coordinator resumes forge land.
Handback records completion at the current HEAD in src/forge/native.py:284–292. However, unbuilt_fix remains true when history contains only start and state commits. This new OR condition therefore bypasses the existing completed-handback exemption and launches another builder round on every resume, preventing close and merge. The existing command test at tests/test_tools_native_work.py:286–289 explicitly requires a round that commits nothing to proceed to close. Apply the completed-round exemption to the new predicate as well.
findings.title: Preserve completed native rounds before starting another build

stop.reason: Owner chose one more round: a builder that finishes without a commit must not start another build.

why: forge land merges a fix that has no code change after a clean review of an empty diff, for example after forge fix amend (GitHub issue 1260).
